## Someone is going to Google you

-   A PI deciding whether to take you on
-   A hiring committee, an agency, a journalist
-   A collaborator who just saw your poster

::: fragment
::: big-statement
**What do they find right now?**
:::
:::

::: notes
~1.5 min. Ask: "Who has Googled themselves lately? What came up?"
If you don't tell your story, search results tell it for you.
:::

## Your story + your proof

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Your website tells

-   What you study and why
-   Who you are
-   How to reach you
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Your GitHub shows

-   Your code and projects
-   How you work
-   That you can build things
:::
:::::

::: {.fragment .card}
A website built on GitHub is already part of your portfolio.
:::

::: notes
~1.5 min. This is the key slide. The site tells, the repos show.
Employers and PIs increasingly look at GitHub as evidence of skills.
:::

## Work in public

::: big-quote
[*To build community, we have to do science publicly, in the open.*](https://javirudolph.github.io/posts/2025-06-19-computational-literacy/)
:::

::: {.fragment .credit}
Inspired by David Robinson, [*The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Public Work*](https://posit.co/resources/videos/the-unreasonable-effectiveness-of-public-work/)
:::

::: notes
~1 min. This quote is from my own blog post about preparing for this job in the open.
The value of your work grows when people can see it.
:::

## Every GitHub account gets **one** personal website:

::: url-main
username.github.io
:::

<br>

Every project you share then lives under it: 

- username.github.io/thesis-maps
- username.github.io/water-quality-dashboard

::: {.fragment .card}
**Choose a username you'd put on a CV.**
:::

::: notes
~1.5 min. Show javirudolph.github.io, then a project under it (javirudolph.github.io/Talks).
:::

# Let's build one {.section-slide}

::: card
[github.com/ARCS-UFLibraries/academic-website-template](https://github.com/ARCS-UFLibraries/academic-website-template)
:::

::: notes
~10 min demo.
1. Show the example site: arcs-uflibraries.github.io/academic-website-template
2. Go to the template repo, click "Use this template", name it username.github.io
3. Settings > Pages > GitHub Actions
4. Edit a FIXME line in _quarto.yml, commit
5. Actions tab: watch the build, open the live site
Backup: have a pre-made site ready in case Wi-Fi is slow.
:::
